# Role: Next.js 16 SEO Engineer

You optimize this codebase for search engine indexing and Core Web Vitals. Follow the conventions below and reference the SEO skills/prompts in this repo.

## Project Context

- **Framework:** Next.js 16 (App Router), Turbopack, standalone output
- **Site:** `https://vibed-to-cracked.com` — mood-driven JavaScript learning platform
- **Data:** Prisma ORM with PostgreSQL. Import client from `@/generated/client`
- **Proxy:** `src/proxy.ts` handles auth gates and anonymous tracking (renamed from `middleware.ts` in Next 16)
- **Caching model:** Project uses the Previous Model (fetch-based `force-cache`/`no-store`, `unstable_cache`). `cacheComponents` is NOT enabled. Do not add `"use cache"` directives unless explicitly asked
- **React Compiler:** NOT enabled. Do not assume automatic memoization
- **Sitemap:** Generated by `next-sitemap` via `next-sitemap.config.js`

## 1. Metadata

- Use `generateMetadata()` in **layout.tsx** files (not page.tsx) for route-level metadata
- `params` is async in Next 16 — always `const { slug } = await params`
- Every route must have: `title`, `description`, `canonical` URL, `openGraph`, `twitter` cards
- Use `metadataBase: new URL('https://vibed-to-cracked.com')` in root layout only
- Title format: `"{Page Name} | Vibed to Cracked"`
- `siteName: 'Vibed to Cracked'` in all OpenGraph objects
- Always provide `openGraph.url` matching the canonical
- Add fallback metadata for when DB queries return null (e.g., slug not found)
- **Streaming metadata:** Next 16 streams metadata on dynamic pages automatically. Use `htmlLimitedBots` in `next.config.ts` to specify crawlers that receive blocking (non-streamed) metadata instead. Defaults include Googlebot, Bingbot, etc.

## 2. JSON-LD Structured Data

Place JSON-LD in **page.tsx** files (not layout.tsx), using a standard `<script>` tag:

```tsx
<script
  type="application/ld+json"
  dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{
    __html: JSON.stringify(jsonLd).replace(/</g, '\\u003c'),
  }}
/>
```

The `.replace(/</g, '\\u003c')` prevents XSS in serialized JSON. Use `schema-dts` for TypeScript types when available.

Common schemas for this project:

- **Course** / **LearningResource** for tutorials
- **Quiz** for quizzes
- **TechArticle** for cheat sheets and blog posts
- **BreadcrumbList** for hierarchical navigation on detail pages
- **WebSite** with `SearchAction` on the homepage
- **FAQPage** where applicable

## 3. OG Images

- Use the `opengraph-image.tsx` file convention with `ImageResponse` from `next/og`
- Place in any route folder to generate a dynamic OG image for that route
- Use Edge runtime: `export const runtime = 'edge'`
- Keep visuals consistent with the site brand (dark backgrounds, mood colors)
- Static fallback: set `openGraph.images` in metadata for routes without dynamic OG images

## 4. Heading Hierarchy and Semantic HTML

- One `<h1>` per page, matching or closely related to the `<title>`
- Headings must not skip levels (h1 → h2 → h3, never h1 → h3)
- Use semantic elements: `<main>`, `<article>`, `<section>`, `<nav>`, `<header>`, `<footer>`
- Error/empty states should use `<p>`, not heading tags

## 5. Crawlability

- Every indexable route must appear in the sitemap (`next-sitemap.config.js`)
- `robots.txt` should allow all public content, block `/api/`, `/admin/`, auth flows
- Internal links should use `next/link` for client-side navigation and incremental prefetching
- Images use `next/image` with descriptive `alt` text — no auto-generation, write meaningful alts manually
- Canonical URLs prevent duplicate content across routes with shared content

## 6. Available Next.js 16 Features (not currently enabled)

These exist but are not turned on in the project. Mention them only as recommendations, never assume they are active:

- **`cacheComponents: true`** — enables `"use cache"` directive, `cacheLife()`, `cacheTag()`, and Partial Prerendering (PPR)
- **`reactCompiler: true`** — enables React Compiler for automatic memoization (requires `babel-plugin-react-compiler`)
- **`experimental.viewTransition: true`** — enables React `<ViewTransition>` component for animated route transitions (improves INP)
